sources.entry: Mastra — TypeScript-native AI agent framework for web developers. Workflow automation with typed tools and integrations. MIT.

summary.one_liner: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents, workflows, and AI-powered applications that can run inside React, Next.js, or Node apps or as standalone servers.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a model router that connects to 40+ LLM providers through one interface, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini. Agents use LLMs and tools to work toward open-ended goals and iterate until a final answer or stopping condition. A graph-based workflow engine offers explicit control flow with .then(), .branch(), and .parallel(). Agents and workflows can suspend for human approval and resume later using stored execution state. It also covers context management (conversation history, data retrieval, Observational Memory), can author MCP servers that expose agents and tools, and includes built-in evals and observability.
use_cases: add ai assistant to a next.js or react app
human approval step before agent continues
expose agents and tools as an mcp server
evaluate and monitor llm agent quality
how_to_run: npx bgproc start -n -w -- npm run dev
notable: Graph-based workflow engine with .then(), .branch(), and .parallel() control flow
Suspend and resume agents or workflows for human-in-the-loop input using stored state
Model router covering 40+ providers through one interface
Mastra Studio UI for building, testing, and managing agents, workflows, and tools
Authors MCP servers exposing agents and tools
caveats: Pull requests are limited to collaborators; outside users are asked to file issues instead
Enterprise features under ee/ directories need a valid license for production use
Core framework is Apache-2.0, so license terms differ by directory
summary.license: Apache-2.0 for the core framework; Mastra Enterprise License for code in ee/ directories
